messages.subject: iid2d vs iidkd
parts:
I am following the example from 3.3.8Correlated effects (iid?d models) from the book by Virgilio Gómez-Rubio. Therefore I have fitted the following models:

nc.new <- data.frame(SID = c(nc.sids$SID74, nc.sids$SID79),
  EXP = c(nc.sids$EXP74, nc.sids$EXP79),
  PERIOD = c(rep("74", 1000), rep("79", 1000)),
  ID = 1:2000)

m.pois.iid2d <- inla(SID ~ 0 + PERIOD + f(ID, model = "iid2d", n = 2 * 1000,
                                          hyper =  list(theta1 = list(param = c(1000, rep(1, 2), rep(0, 2*(2-1)/2))))
                                          ),
  data = nc.new, family = "poisson", control.compute = list(dic = FALSE, return.marginals=TRUE, config=TRUE, waic = TRUE))

m.pois.iidkd <- inla(SID ~ 0 + PERIOD + f(ID, model = "iidkd", order=2, n = 2 * 1000,
                                          hyper =  list(theta1 = list(param = c(1000, rep(1, 2), rep(0, 2*(2-1)/2))))
                                          ),
  data = nc.new, family = "poisson", control.compute = list(dic = FALSE, return.marginals=TRUE, config=TRUE, waic = TRUE))

My struggle is the interpretation of the parameters. For the first model I obtain:

Fixed effects:
                  mean    
PERIOD74 1.612 0.026
PERIOD79 1.612 0.026 

Random effects:
  Name   Model
    ID IID2D model

Model hyperparameters:
                                                 mean    
Precision for ID (component 1) 2.535 
Precision for ID (component 2) 2.537 
Rho1:2 for ID                            0.997 

And for the second:

Fixed effects:
                 mean  
PERIOD74 2.016 
PERIOD79 2.016 

Random effects:
  Name   Model
    ID IIDKD model

Model hyperparameters:
                      mean    
Theta1 for ID  3.41 
Theta2 for ID  3.41 
Theta3 for ID -2.88 

As I would very much like to sample the variance and correlations in a similar manner as one can do with inla.posterior.sample, it would be very useful to be able to use the function inla.iidkd.sample to obtain the matrix and then report that for each sampling. However, when the results differ so significantly, I am not certain how to proceed with the iidkd model. Any ideas on why the results differ so much, and how I can sample the variance and correlation of a iidkd model?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] iid2d vs iidkd
parts:
the iidkd is a new and better implementation, please use that one and
not iid2d.

you need to use sampling to convert the fitted parameters into var and
cov and correlation; see

see the example at the end of

inla.doc("iidkd")

for how to do this
